requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp electronics, LED modules on PCB) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz), and constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band (decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz), and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed a pulse amplitude of +75 V (positive polarity) and -100 V (negative polarity).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed a pulse amplitude of +150 V (positive polarity) and -450 V (negative polarity).
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The ESA shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation at the test levels in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band of Table 2a: stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz), TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz), BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz), ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz), reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).

The ESA shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation at the minimum test levels over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band of Table 2b: stripline 50 V/m, TEM cell 62.5 V/m, BCI 50 mA, ALSE 25 V/m (below 2 GHz) and 8 V/m (above 2 GHz), reverberation chamber 18 V/m (below 2 GHz) and 6 V/m (above 2 GHz).

The ESA shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements only if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" (including stop lamp and rear position lamp operation).

The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

For immunity to test pulse 1, the ESA shall be tested at -75 V (12 V system) / -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses, with functional performance status III for both immunity related and non-immunity related functions.

For immunity to test pulse 2a, the ESA shall be tested at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, with functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity.

For immunity to test pulse 2b, the ESA shall be tested at +10 V (12 V system) / +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, with functional performance status II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity.

For immunity to test pulse 3a, the ESA shall be tested at -112 V (12 V system) / -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity.

For immunity to test pulse 3b, the ESA shall be tested at +75 V (12 V system) / +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, with functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity.

For immunity to the starting profile (level II, 10 pulses), an ESA installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor shall achieve functional status B for immunity related functions (if it shall be operational during engine start phases, otherwise C) and D for functions not related to immunity.
ESAs approved under UN Regulation No. 10 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved.

The external surface of the vehicle, including the lighting and light-signalling devices, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of the vehicle, including the lighting and light-signalling devices, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
No protruding part of the external surface, including the lighting and light-signalling devices, shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.

Parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm are not subject to the 2.5 mm radius requirement, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, the hardness measurement being taken with the component as installed on the vehicle.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in annex 3 to UN Regulation No. 42, the lighting and signalling devices shall continue to operate correctly and to remain visible.

After each impact test made in accordance with annex 3 to UN Regulation No. 42, should the adjustment of the factory-fitted lighting devices be disturbed, it may be corrected to conform to the required specifications only provided this can be done by the normal means of adjustment.
Each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 148.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps must be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.

When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each of these lamps satisfies the provisions set out in UN Regulation No. 148 or in another Regulation; lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of such unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source).

Alternatively, in the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the lamp shall be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

If the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates a manufacturer logo, only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components may be incorporated, and all requirements for the specific function of UN Regulation No. 148 shall be fulfilled.
If a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.

If a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.

Alternatively, in case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8. and 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced, and the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
All measurements, photometric and colorimetric, shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8. of UN Regulation No. 148 and the methods of measurement given in Annex 3.
In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

In case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements shall be made separately, in accordance with each applicable condition, and all separate measurement results shall be added together.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

In the case where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.

In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.

In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for maximum intensity if all lamps together are lit.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp: for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, under night-time conditions; for other systems, under standard conditions.

If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.

If one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated rear position and stop lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the 5:1 ratio are those obtained with all sources in operation.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, applying the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid no sharp variation of colour shall be observed.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of a rear position lamp of category R1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd on the reference axis, a maximum luminous intensity of 17 cd when used as a single lamp or 8.5 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, and have a minimum luminous intensity of 0.05 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of a rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd on the reference axis, a maximum luminous intensity of 42 cd when used as a single lamp or 21 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, and have a minimum luminous intensity of 0.05 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1.
For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 60 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The minimum luminous intensity of the rear position lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as given in Table 4 (0.05 cd).
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of a stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 60 cd on the reference axis, a maximum luminous intensity of 260 cd when used as a single lamp or 130 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, and have a minimum luminous intensity of 0.3 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of a stop lamp of category S2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 60 cd on the reference axis, a maximum luminous intensity of 730 cd when used as a single lamp or 365 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, and have a minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 of 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night).
The minimum luminous intensity of the stop lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as given in Table 7.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of a reversing lamp (category AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 80 cd on the reference axis and meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V.
The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed 300 cd in or above the H-plane.
The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed 600 cd below the H-plane, down to 5°D.
The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (category AR) shall not exceed 8,000 cd below 5°D.

In the case where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a photometric value of at least 25 cd shall be satisfied.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

The rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above and 15° below vertically; reduced angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard apply only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, and 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.

The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard horizontally and 15° above and 15° below vertically; reduced angles of 20° inboard / 45° outboard apply only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, and 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.

The values shown in the light distribution figures give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

In the case where a rear position lamp or a stop lamp of category S1, S2 is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern should be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.

In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of a lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.

For rear position lamps and stop lamps (S1, S2), the luminous intensity in the various directions of measurement shall be not less than the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Figure A3-I.
For reversing lamps, the luminous intensity at the measuring points shall be not less than the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.

For reversing lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For rear position lamps and stop lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
For front and rear position lamps, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
For stop lamps, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
For reversing lamps, the luminous intensity distribution shall additionally be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Lamps with non-replaceable light sources, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.

In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant, the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage, and the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN Regulation No. 148.

In conformity of production, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN Regulation No. 148, and for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3 the measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12.
In conformity of production, the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of UN Regulation No. 148.

The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, these must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.

For testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

After verification of the general specifications and the specifications of shape and dimensions, the ten samples of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and at least one hour after this test examined as to their colorimetric characteristics and RI for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, and the two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall then be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.

The Class IA or IB retro-reflector samples of the first group shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The Class IA or IB retro-reflector samples of the second group shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector samples of the third group shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The Class IA or IB retro-reflector samples of the fourth group shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

In the case where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified.

For photometric measurements of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of red Class IA and IB retro-reflectors at an angle of divergence of 20' must be equal to or greater than 300 mcd/lx at illumination angle β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 200 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and 100 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of red Class IA and IB retro-reflectors at an angle of divergence of 1°30' must be equal to or greater than 5 mcd/lx at illumination angle β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 2.8 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and 2.5 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of white Class IA and IB retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than 1,200 / 800 / 400 mcd/lx at an angle of divergence of 20' and 20 / 11.2 / 10 mcd/lx at 1°30', for illumination angles (β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°) / (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) / (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°) respectively.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of amber Class IA and IB retro-reflectors must be equal to or greater than 750 / 500 / 250 mcd/lx at an angle of divergence of 20' and 12.5 / 7 / 6.25 mcd/lx at 1°30', for illumination angles (β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°) / (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) / (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°) respectively.

RI values of the retro-reflector lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

In the case where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The testing of the colour for the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

A retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
All markings on the retro-reflective device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
Retro-reflectors approved under UN Regulation No. 150 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
In conformity of production, the chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflector shall be complied with.

When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device, and if there is any such effect, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5.

When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the minimum-RI value of ε; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0° and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°, and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
The measuring distance for the photometry of the retro-reflector shall be chosen such that the limits for the angles δ ≤ 10', γ ≤ 10' and η ≤ 80' are respected, but not lower than 10 m.
The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, with max/min ≤ 1.05.
The shape of the illuminating surfaces of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape from an observation distance of 10 metres.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.

Retro-reflective devices, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water; the test shall be repeated after turning the device through 180°, and the sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection after the water penetration test clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

If visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2., the device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.

As an alternative for retro-reflective devices of Class IB, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Part 3 of Annex 6 shall be applied instead of the water penetration test.

The water spray cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) which provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, with the centreline of the nozzle(s) directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
The rotating test platform for the moisture test shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.

The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector of height 100 mm and minimum inside diameter 140 mm centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform.
A sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the water spray.
During the water spray test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.

Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation, and no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
Upon completion of the drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.

A sample device, mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust in the dust exposure test chamber using fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84.
During the dust exposure test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.

The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and the test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours.
Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.

Retro-reflective devices must be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
For mirror-backed moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB with an accessible rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After brushing the rear face of a Class IA or IB moulded plastics retro-reflector, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, then removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
The RI of the retro-reflector shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2., after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.

The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013, shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
In the case of retro-reflective devices, the samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.

For resistance to fuels, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.
After about five minutes following the fuel test, the surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

For resistance to lubricating oils, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil, and after about 5 minutes the surface shall be cleaned and the RI measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.

The light emitted by red lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp) shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) inside the "red" chromaticity area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line, R41 purple boundary y = 0.980 – x (intersection points R1 0.645/0.335, R2 0.665/0.335, R3 0.735/0.265, R4 0.721/0.259).

The light emitted by white lamps (reversing lamp) shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) inside the "white" chromaticity area defined by the boundaries W12 green boundary y = 0.150 + 0.640 x, W23 yellowish green boundary y = 0.440, W34 yellow boundary x = 0.500, W45 reddish purple boundary y = 0.382, W56 purple boundary y = 0.050 + 0.750 x, W61 blue boundary x = 0.310.

The night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from the red rear retro-reflector shall have chromaticity coordinates (x,y) inside the "red" area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line, R41 purple boundary y = 0.978 - x (intersection points R1 0.643/0.335, R2 0.665/0.335, R3 0.735/0.265, R4 0.720/0.258).

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 48.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, and parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle (except side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps), with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.

In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are not permitted to be reciprocally incorporated.

Single lamps whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts shall be installed in such a way that the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection.

Alternatively, single lamps whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts shall be installed in such a way that the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
The maximum height of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of a lamp as regards width shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement on red light visible to the front shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors shall be prohibited.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN Regulation No. 48.

Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component, additional lamps for these functions switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN Regulation No. 48.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

If it is not practicable to keep the apparent surface hidden by not more than 50 per cent, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate and the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.
During a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are allowed provided that the intensity of all such lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are allowed provided that, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, is maintained throughout variation transitions.

Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity of category R2 and S2 lamps is allowed only within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface.

Independent from environmental conditions, a decrease of the luminous intensity of category R2 and S2 lamps, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed only as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m; as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h the intensity decrease already activated may remain active.
No sharp variation of intensity of variable-intensity lamps shall be observed during transition.

For vehicles of M and N categories, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

For vehicles of M and N categories, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, no account being taken of obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
A LED module does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48 when installed on a vehicle.
In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources unless they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
The reversing lamp is mandatory on motor vehicles.
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional.
The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be, in height, not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.
For a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, where there are two devices, the geometric visibility shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The orientation of the reversing lamp shall be rearwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system cannot operate.
For the reversing lamp, a tell-tale is optional; however a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories are mandatory on all categories of vehicles.
Two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges.

S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

The horizontal angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for stop lamps mounted below 750 mm the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the stop lamps shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
For the stop lamps, a tell-tale is optional; however a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamp devices of R or R1 or R2 categories are mandatory.
Two rear position lamps shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For the rear position lamp, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for M1 and N1 category vehicles there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces.

The rear position lamps shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
The rear position lamps shall be, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

The horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be horizontally 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle reducible to 20° under the H plane if mounted below 750 mm) and vertically 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle reducible to 5° if mounted below 750 mm).

Under the alternative geometric visibility for M1 and N1 vehicles, to be considered visible the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
The orientation of the rear position lamps shall be rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.

A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps is mandatory and shall be combined with that of the front position lamps (not applicable when daytime running lamps are switched ON); a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mandatory on motor vehicles.

Two rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be fitted, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

For the rear retro-reflector, that point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for M1 and N1 category vehicles there is no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges.

The rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm, or not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), or 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
The rear retro-reflector shall be, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall be horizontally 30° inwards and outwards and vertically 10° above and below horizontal, except that where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
